<module id="serial2parallel">
    <description>Serial-to-Parallel Conversion Circuit</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="din_serial">Serial input data.</input>
        <input id="din_valid">Validity signal for input data.</input>
        <output id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data (8 bits wide).</output>
        <output id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">State IDLE.</parameter>
        <parameter id="RECEIVE">State RECEIVE.</parameter>
        <parameter id="OUTPUT">State OUTPUT.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[3:0]">Counter to keep track of the number of serial input data bits received.</reg>
        <reg id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data register.</reg>
        <reg id="dout_valid">Valid output signal register.</reg>
        
        <always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)>
            if (~rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 4'd0;
                dout_parallel <= 8'd0;
                dout_valid <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                case(cnt)
                    4'd0: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            dout_parallel[7] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd1: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            dout_parallel[6] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd2: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            dout_parallel[5] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd3: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            dout_parallel[4] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd4: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            dout_parallel[3] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd5: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            dout_parallel[2] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd6: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            dout_parallel[1] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd7: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            dout_parallel[0] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    default: begin
                        cnt <= 4'd0;
                        dout_valid <= 1'b1;
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
        
        <always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)> // Output valid signal
            if (~rst_n) begin
                dout_valid <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if(cnt == 4'd7 && din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                    dout_valid <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    dout_valid <= 1'b0;
                end
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of the clock or negative edge of the reset signal. If the reset signal is active, the counter is initialized to 0, the parallel output data is cleared, and the output valid signal is set to 0. Otherwise, based on the current value of the counter, the corresponding bit of the parallel output data is updated with the serial input data. After receiving 8 serial input data bits, the output valid signal is set to 1, indicating that the parallel output data is valid. If the counter reaches its maximum value, it resets to 0.</implementation>
</module>
